title: Derivative rules (sum, product, quotient)
goal: Use the power, sum, product, and quotient rules to find derivatives in seconds instead of setting up a limit every time.

beforeThis.skill: Save yourself work: rewrite roots as fractional powers ($\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}$) and denominators as negative powers ($\frac{1}{x^3} = x^{-3}$) before differentiating!

links.label: Precalculus: Power functions and fractional exponents

questions.asking: Check if the derivative of a sum of two differentiable functions is always the sum of their derivatives.
questions.statement: True or false: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\{f(x) + g(x)\} = f'(x) + g'(x)$ when $f$ and $g$ are differentiable functions.

questions.asking: Test with a simple example like $f(x) = x$ and $g(x) = x$: the product rule needs $f'g + fg'$, not just $f'g'$!
questions.statement: True or false: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\{f(x)g(x)\} = f'(x)g'(x)$ when $f$ and $g$ are differentiable functions.

questions.asking: Check whether the written two-term expression for the derivative of $f(x)/g(x)$ is algebraically equivalent to the standard derivative of a quotient.
questions.statement: True or false: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left\{\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right\} = \dfrac{f'(x)}{g(x)} - \dfrac{f(x)g'(x)}{g^2(x)}$ when $f$ and $g$ are differentiable functions.

questions.asking: Compute $g'(x)$ for $g(x) = 3f(x)$ in three different ways (such as writing $3f(x)$ as $f(x)+f(x)+f(x)$, as a product $3 \cdot f(x)$, or as a quotient $f(x)/(1/3)$) and confirm all three match.
questions.statement: Let $f$ be a differentiable function. Use at least three different rules to differentiate $g(x) = 3f(x)$ in different ways, and verify that they all give the same answer.

questions.asking: Rewrite $\sqrt{x}$ as $x^{1/2}$, then either use the product rule $(fg)' = f'g + fg'$ or FOIL the brackets first and use the power rule.
Find the particle's speed, direction of motion, and whether its speed is increasing or decreasing at $t = 2$ from its position function $x(t)$.
questions.statement:
A particle moves along the $x$-axis so that its position at time $t$ is given by $x = t^3 - 4t^2 + 1$.

  1. At $t = 2$, what is the particle’s speed? That is, what is the absolute value of its velocity?
  2. At $t = 2$, in what direction is the particle moving?
  3. At $t = 2$, is the particle’s speed increasing or decreasing?

questions.asking: Apply the quotient rule $\frac{\text{low}\cdot d(\text{high}) - \text{high}\cdot d(\text{low})}{(\text{low})^2}$ and combine the terms on top.
Write a simplified formula for the derivative of $g(x) = f(x)e^x$ in terms of $f(x)$, $f'(x)$, and $e^x$.
questions.statement: Let $g(x) = f(x)e^x$, for a differentiable function $f(x)$. Give a simplified formula for $g'(x)$. Functions of the form $g(x)$ are relatively common. If you remember this formula, you can save yourself some time when you need to differentiate them.

questions.asking: Write an expression in terms of $b'(t)$ and $d'(t)$ for the rate at which the town's population is changing at time $t$.
questions.statement: A town is founded in the year 2000. After $t$ years, it has had $b(t)$ births and $d(t)$ deaths. Nobody enters or leaves the town except by birth or death (whoa). Give an expression for the rate the population of the town is growing.

questions.asking: Find the coordinates $(x, y)$ of every point on the parabola $y = 3x^2$ whose tangent line passes through $(2, 9)$.
questions.statement: Find all points on the curve $y = 3x^2$ where the tangent line passes through $(2, 9)$.

questions.asking: Write a formula in terms of $t$ for the rate of change of the rectangle's area (in $\text{m}^2/\text{s}$) at any time $t > 0$.
questions.statement: A rectangle is growing. At time $t = 0$, it is a square with side length $1$ metre. Its width increases at a constant rate of $2$ metres per second, and its length increases at a constant rate of $5$ metres per second. How fast is its area increasing at time $t > 0$?

questions.asking: Find the constants $a$ and $b$ so that the two pieces of $f(x)$ have the same height and the same derivative at $x = 1$.
questions.statement:
Find constants $a, b$ so that the following function is differentiable:

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} ax^2 + b & x \le 1 \\ e^x & x > 1 \end{cases}$$
